Unit circle radius in plot coordinates radius_val = axes.c2p(1, 0)[0] - axes.c2p(0, 0)[0] circle = Circle(radius=radius_val, color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.3) circle.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0)) # Labels for 1 and -1 label_1 = Text("1", font_size=20, color=WHITE) label_1.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), UR, buff=0.1) label_neg1 = Text("-1", font_size=20, color=WHITE) label_neg1.next_to(axes.c2p(-1, 0), UL, buff=0.1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 === # Description: Show the unit circle with a marker starting at 1 on the real axis. self.lecture[0].set_color(color_travel) marker = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 0), color=color_travel) self.play( Create(axes), Create(circle), Write(label_1), FadeIn(marker) ) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 === # Description: Move the marker along the top half of the circle's circumference. self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE) self.lecture[1].set_color(color_half_turn) arc_path = Arc( radius=radius_val, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=color_half_turn, stroke_width=4 ) # Position the arc correctly arc_path.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN) self.play( MoveAlongPath(marker, arc_path), Create(arc_path), run_time=3, rate_func=linear ) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 === # Description: The marker lands at -1 on the real axis, highlighting the value in red (#FF0000). self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE) self.lecture[2].set_color(color_land) # Equation from Issue 36: scale 0.9, area E3-F5 equation = Text("e^iπ = -1", color=color_land, font_size=32) self.place_in_area(equation, "E3", "F5", scale_factor=0.9) self.play( marker.animate.set_color(color_land), label_neg1.animate.set_color(color_land), Write(label_neg1), Write(equation) ) self.wait(2) from manim import * import numpy as np class TeachingScene(Scene): def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines): # BASE self.camera.background_color = "#000000" self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP) self.add(self.title) # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-") lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines] self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8) self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2) self.add(self.lecture) # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side) self.grid = {} rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"] # Top to bottom cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"] # Left to right for i, row in enumerate(rows): for j, col in enumerate(cols): x = 0.5 + j * 1 y = 2.2 - i * 1 self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0]) def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0): mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos]) return mobject def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0): tl_pos = self.grid[top_left] br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right] # Calculate center of the area center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2 center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2 center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0]) mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(center) return mobject class Section6Scene(TeachingScene): def construct(self): # Data from storyboard title_text = "Summary: Elegance in Unity" lecture_lines = [ "Consider five fundamental constants of the mathematical universe.", "They unite perfectly in this one simple, elegant statement.", "Zero, one, e, i, and pi combined forever.", "This formula is the golden key to mathematical harmony.", "We have reached the bridge: elegance in unity." ] # Initialize layout self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines) # Colors for the constants and assets COLOR_E = "#88CA5E" COLOR_PI = "#FF9D00" COLOR_I = "#58C4DD" COLOR_1 = "#FFFFFF" COLOR_0 = "#FFFFFF" COLOR_KEY = "#FFD700" # Asset path for the golden key icon key_path = "/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg" # Initialize the parts of the constants for Animation 1 char_e = Text("e", color=COLOR_E) char_i = Text("i", color=COLOR_I) char_pi = Text("π", color=COLOR_PI) char_one = Text("1", color=COLOR_1) char_zero = Text("0", color=COLOR_0) # Target formula parts for Animation 2 morphing # We construct the formula from individual Text objects to allow precise morphing and coloring. t_e = Text("e", color=COLOR_E) t_exp = Text("^(", color=WHITE) t_i = Text("i", color=COLOR_I) t_pi = Text("π", color=COLOR_PI) t_paren_r = Text(")", color=WHITE) t_plus = Text(" + ", color=WHITE) t_one = Text("1", color=COLOR_1) t_equals = Text(" = ", color=WHITE) t_zero = Text("0", color=COLOR_0) # Group formula parts and position it using place_in_area as per Issue 38 # We don't add them yet; they serve as targets for ReplacementTransform. formula_group = VGroup(t_e, t_exp, t_i, t_pi, t_paren_r, t_plus, t_one, t_equals, t_zero).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1) # Fixed spatial balance issue as per Issue 38 instruction self.place_in_area(formula_group, 'C1', 'D6', scale_factor=1.0) # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 === # Script: "Consider five fundamental constants of the mathematical universe." # Action: Arrange the symbols 0, 1, e, i, and pi randomly on the screen. self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW) # Place constants at random grid points on the right side self.place_at_grid(char_e, "B2", scale_factor=1.2) self.place_at_grid(char_i, "E4", scale_factor=1.2) self.place_at_grid(char_pi, "C5", scale_factor=1.2) self.place_at_grid(char_one, "B5", scale_factor=1.2) self.place_at_grid(char_zero, "E2", scale_factor=1.2) self.play( FadeIn(char_e), FadeIn(char_i), FadeIn(char_pi), FadeIn(char_one), FadeIn(char_zero), run_time=2 ) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 === # Script: "They unite perfectly in this one simple, elegant statement." # Action: Morph the layout into the structured equation e^{i*pi} + 1 = 0. self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE) self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW) self.play( ReplacementTransform(char_e, t_e), ReplacementTransform(char_i, t_i), ReplacementTransform(char_pi, t_pi), ReplacementTransform(char_one, t_one), ReplacementTransform(char_zero, t_zero), FadeIn(t_exp), FadeIn(t_paren_r), FadeIn(t_plus), FadeIn(t_equals), run_time=2 ) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 === # Script: "Zero, one, e, i, and pi combined forever." # Action: Flash each constant in its unique color. self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE) self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW) # Flashing each constant in parallel to emphasize their distinct identities self.play( Indicate(t_e, color=COLOR_E), Indicate(t_i, color=COLOR_I), Indicate(t_pi, color=COLOR_PI), Indicate(t_one, color=COLOR_1), Indicate(t_zero, color=COLOR_0), run_time=2 ) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 === # Script: "This formula is the golden key to mathematical harmony." # Action: Transform the equation into a single glowing golden key icon. self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE) self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW) # Asset integration (Issue 24/44): Load and place the golden key SVG key_icon = SVGMobject(key_path, color=COLOR_KEY) # Centering the key icon in a prominent central area of the grid self.place_in_area(key_icon, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.2) # All currently visible parts of the formula everything_formula = VGroup(t_e, t_exp, t_i, t_pi, t_paren_r, t_plus, t_one, t_equals, t_zero) self.play( ReplacementTransform(everything_formula, key_icon), run_time=2 ) # Adding a visual pulse to simulate "glowing" self.play(Indicate(key_icon, color=YELLOW_A), run_time=1) self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 === # Script: "We have reached the bridge: elegance in unity." # outline.topic: The Most Beautiful Bridge: Understanding Euler's Formula
outline.target_audience: Advanced high school students or first-year university students

sections.title: The Grand Collision of Worlds
sections.content: Introduce the characters: 'e' (the king of growth), 'pi' (the lord of circles), and 'i' (the imaginary phantom). Explain that these three seem unrelated until a single formula bridges them. Use a visual of three separate islands merging into one.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Mathematical Explorer' standing at a crossroads where three paths labeled Calculus, Trigonometry, and Complex Numbers meet at a single signpost: e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Hidden Power of 'i'
sections.content: Review 'i' not just as the square root of -1, but as a geometric '90-degree rotation operator' on the complex plane. Show that multiplying by 'i' turns a vector from the x-axis to the y-axis.
sections.example: An arrow on a compass pointing at '1' (East). Multiplying by 'i' rotates the compass needle to point at 'i' (North). Multiplying again by 'i' points to '-1' (West).

sections.title: The Engine: Continuous Growth in a New Direction
sections.content: Explain that 'e' represents continuous growth. While e^x grows outward, e^(ix) grows 'sideways' because 'i' keeps rotating the direction of growth perpendicular to the current position.
sections.example: A small steering drone. Usually, it pushes forward (real growth). But with 'i' as the pilot, it always pushes at a right angle to its path, forcing the drone into a perfect circular orbit.

sections.title: Mapping the Circle: Euler's General Formula
sections.content: Introduce e^(ix) = cos(x) + i*sin(x). Use an animation of a point moving around the unit circle. Show the horizontal component (cos) and the vertical component (sin) being tracked as the angle 'x' increases.
sections.example: A lighthouse beam. The distance from the center is always 1. As the beam rotates by angle 'x', its coordinates are simply the cosine and sine values mapped onto the complex plane.

sections.title: The Final Destination: pi i
sections.content: Plug 'pi' into the formula. Since 'pi' represents a 180-degree turn in radians, the rotation reaches the exact opposite side of the starting point (1) on the circle.
sections.example: The 'Mathematical Explorer' walks halfway around the circle (pi distance). They started at 1 on the right side; after traveling a distance of pi along the arc, they are standing exactly at -1 on the left side.

sections.title: Summary: Elegance in Unity
sections.content: Conclude by showing the full equation e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0. Highlight how it combines five fundamental constants: 0, 1, e, i, and pi in one simple statement.
sections.example: A visual puzzle where five pieces labeled with the constants click together to form a perfect golden key, symbolizing the unity of mathematical disciplines.

storyboard.title: The Grand Collision of Worlds
lecture_lines: Meet e, pi, and i: three separate mathematical worlds.
For centuries, these constants appeared completely unrelated.
But a hidden bridge exists between these distant islands.
Let's explore the signpost where these paths finally meet.
This is Euler’s formula, the most beautiful in math.
animations: Display three floating 'islands' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/island.svg] with 'e' (#88CA5E), 'pi' (#FF9D00), and 'i' (#58C4DD) symbols.
Animate the islands [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/island.svg] drifting closer together on a black background.
Merge the islands [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/island.svg] into a single, unified landscape with a golden glow (#FFD700).
Place a signpost [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/signpost.svg] in the center of the merged landscape.
Fade in the formula e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0 on the signpost [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/signpost.svg] in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Hidden Power of 'i'
lecture_lines: In math, i is the root of negative one.
Geometrically, multiplying by i creates a ninety-degree rotation.
It turns a horizontal real number into a vertical one.
animations: Draw a complex plane; show a white arrow (#FFFFFF) pointing from origin to 1.
Rotate the white arrow 90 degrees to point at 'i' (#58C4DD).
Rotate the arrow another 90 degrees to point at -1 (#FF0000).

storyboard.title: The Engine: Continuous Growth in a New Direction
lecture_lines: The number e typically represents continuous exponential growth.
Multiplying by i rotates this growth by ninety degrees.
This constant turning forces the path into a perfect circle.
animations: Show the engine icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/engine.svg] at (1,0) on a complex plane with a small velocity vector.
Rotate the velocity vector to always be 90 degrees relative to the engine's position from origin.
The engine icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/engine.svg] moves, tracing a white circle (#FFFFFF) as it continuously 'grows' sideways.

storyboard.title: Mapping the Circle: Euler's General Formula
lecture_lines: Euler’s formula maps this circular path on a plane.
The expression e to the ix tracks our position.
Cosine measures how far we are horizontally.
Sine measures our vertical height on the complex plane.
Together, they define every point on the unit circle.
animations: Show a unit circle on the complex plane with a radius line at angle 'x'.
Project a green line (#88CA5E) onto the real axis, labeled 'cos(x)'.
Project a blue line (#58C4DD) onto the imaginary axis, labeled 'i*sin(x)'.
Display the equation e^{ix} = cos(x) + i*sin(x) in the corner.
Animate the radius line rotating, showing the cos and sin lengths changing.

storyboard.title: The Final Destination: pi i
lecture_lines: Now, we travel a distance of exactly pi.
This path covers half of the unit circle's circumference.
We land precisely at negative one on the complex plane.
animations: Show the unit circle with a marker starting at 1 on the real axis.
Move the marker along the top half of the circle's circumference.
The marker lands at -1 on the real axis, highlighting the value in red (#FF0000).

storyboard.title: Summary: Elegance in Unity
lecture_lines: Consider five fundamental constants of the mathematical universe.
They unite perfectly in this one simple, elegant statement.
Zero, one, e, i, and pi combined forever.
This formula is the golden key to mathematical harmony.
We have reached the bridge: elegance in unity.
animations: Arrange the symbols 0, 1, e, i, and pi randomly on the screen.
Morph the layout into the structured equation e^{i*pi} + 1 = 0.
Flash each constant in its unique color (e:#88CA5E, pi:#FF9D00, i:#58C4DD, 1:#FFFFFF, 0:#FFFFFF).
Transform the entire equation into a single glowing golden key (#FFD700) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg].
Fade in the title 'Elegance in Unity' below the golden key [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg].

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The 'i sin(x)' label is positioned too far to the left of the complex plane, losing its visual proximity to the blue vertical sine segment. Fix: Line 92: self.place_at_grid(i_sin_label, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=92, object=i_sin_label)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The 'cos(x)' label is positioned too low below the horizontal axis, which weakens the association with the green cosine segment. Fix: Line 85: self.place_at_grid(cos_label, 'E5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=85, object=cos_label)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The concluding equation is positioned too low in the grid and is scaled too large (1.2), causing it to appear cramped against the bottom frame edge. Fix: Line 137: self.place_in_area(equation, 'E3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=137, object=equation)
issues.resolution_note: Equation positioned in area E3-F5 with scale 0.9 as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The axes object occupies four vertical grid rows (B-E), leaving insufficient breathing room for the final formula at the bottom. Fix: Line 75: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'D6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=75, object=axes)
issues.resolution_note: Axes positioned in area B2-D6 with scale 0.8 to provide more space for the equation.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_6] Problem: The horizontally extensive formula 'e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0' is currently placed at a single grid point (C3) with a large scale factor (2.0), which causes it to crowd the right-side margins and results in poor spatial balance within the 6x6 grid. Fix: Line 67: self.place_in_area(formula, 'C1', 'D6', scale_factor=1.0) (line=67, object=formula)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed spatial balance of the formula by using place_in_area('C1', 'D6') with a scale_factor of 1.0.

improvements.problem: The island_i asset is placed at the extreme edge (B6), which risks being cut off on different screen aspect ratios and creates visual imbalance.
The landscape area (C2-E5) starts too close to the left side, potentially obstructing the long lecture line 'Meet i, the mysterious imaginary phantom.'
The Euler's formula at 0.8 scale is too small within the landscape box, making it difficult to read relative to the title and lecture lines.
The coordinate plane is positioned such that the top row of the right-side grid (Row A) is entirely unused, making the layout appear slightly unbalanced and bottom-heavy.
improvements.solution: Line 71: Change the area from 'B2-F6' to 'A2-F6' and increase the scale to 0.9 to better utilize vertical space and improve the visual balance of the right-hand panel.

improvements.problem: The labels 'i', '1', and '-1' are relatively small and sit very close to the axis tick marks and vector arrowheads, which may reduce legibility on smaller screens.
improvements.solution: Line 71: Increasing the scale_factor of the plane to 0.9 within the 'A2-F6' area will naturally enlarge these labels and provide better spacing between the axes and the vector elements.

improvements.problem: The e_label at B4 directly overlaps with the growth path (the orange arrow and white circle) when it reaches its maximum vertical point at the top of the rotation.
The i_label at B5 is positioned within the plane's active animation area, causing visual obstruction as the growth path rotates through the top-right quadrant.
The vertical space in Row A is underutilized, while the labels in Row B create a crowded appearance at the top edge of the complex plane.
improvements.solution: Move labels to Row A to create a clear 'header' area for conceptual components, maintaining a 1-grid-unit distance from the plane's boundary (B2-F6).

improvements.problem: The imaginary axis label 'Im' overlaps with the label 'e to the ix' as the point moves along the circular path in the upper quadrant.
The 'i sin(x)' label is positioned too far to the left of the complex plane, losing its visual proximity to the blue vertical sine segment.
The 'cos(x)' label is positioned too low below the horizontal axis, which weakens the association with the green cosine segment.
The concluding equation is positioned too low in the grid and is scaled too large (1.2), causing it to appear cramped against the bottom frame edge.
The axes object occupies four vertical grid rows (B-E), leaving insufficient breathing room for the final formula at the bottom.

The horizontally extensive formula 'e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0' is currently placed at a single grid point (C3) with a large scale factor (2.0), which causes it to crowd the right-side margins and results in poor spatial balance within the 6x6 grid.
